title: TCP: Introduce a Distal Algorithm for disambiguating Retransmissions
description:
The historic disambiguation for classifying (Fast) Retransmissions
and Out of Orders hardly satisfies all cases as it is rather
designed for server-side captures.

Introduce a more neutral alternative algorithm based on an elder
history (hence the name distal) rather than the last few
Duplicate Acks seen.

Fast Recovery (with or without SACK permission) then comes with
more affinity towards Retransmissions than Out of Orders.

Fix #10725 #20673

changes_data.diff:
@@ -712,12 +712,30 @@ Supersedes “TCP Dup ACK”.
 
 // TCP_A_AMBIGUOUS_INTERPRETATIONS
 [discrete]
-==== TCP Ambiguous Interpretations
+==== TCP Ambiguous Interpretations and the Classification Dilemma
 
 Some captures are quite difficult to analyze automatically, particularly when the
 time frame may cover both Fast Retransmission and Out-Of-Order packets. A TCP
-preference allows to switch the precedence of these two interpretations at the
-protocol level.
+preference (Fast Retransmission supersedes Out-of-Order interpretation) allows to
+switch the precedence of these two interpretations at the protocol level.
+
+In addition, interpretations may be different whether the capture was
+performed server side, client side or anywhere in the middle. While the historical
+classification algorithm is comparing new packets to almost previous, adjacent
+Duplicate ACKs, the “Enable Distal Disambiguation Algorithm” TCP preference allows
+a more neutral interpretation if the iRTT is known
+(the 3WHS is present in the capture).
+In this case, the time interval between a missing packet is compared to its
+supposed retransmission and if it's between 0,8 and 2,4 it will be considered as
+a Fast Retransmission if enough Duplicate ACKs were seen. In other cases (not so
+many Duplicate ACKs seen), packets are considered as a Retransmission (RTO) if
+the time is over the 2,4 ratio. Otherwise, they are Out-of-Order ones.
+
+[NOTE]
+====
+While RFC 6675 is taken into account in Wireshark's implementation of Duplicate
+ACKs, RFC 5827 and 8985 aren't for now.
+====
 
 // TCP_A_CONVERSATION_COMPLETENESS
 [discrete]
